candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: provide medication education, distinguish prescribed therapies from non-equivalent products, and evaluate therapeutic response.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — prescription icosapent ethyl versus OTC fish oil
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish prescription icosapent ethyl from nonprescription fish-oil supplements: it is a standardized EPA medication with defined dosing and evidence, and OTC products should not be substituted as if they were dose-for-dose equivalents.

options.A: This is a prescription EPA formulation with a defined dose and indication; nonprescription fish-oil supplements are not considered equivalent substitutes and may have variable fatty-acid content.
options.B: Any over-the-counter fish-oil capsule can be substituted dose-for-dose because all omega-3 products have standardized EPA content and identical evidence.
options.C: The medication is prescribed mainly to lower blood pressure and has little expected effect on triglycerides.
options.D: Icosapent ethyl is an EPA-plus-DHA product, so a rise in LDL-C from its DHA component is required for the medication to work.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA labeling identifies icosapent ethyl as a prescription ethyl ester of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) indicated, among other labeled uses, as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia. The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline explicitly states that nonprescription fish-oil supplements are not equivalent to prescription omega-3 medications and have variable fatty-acid content. B therefore makes an unsafe equivalence. C misstates the treatment purpose in this scenario. D is incorrect because icosapent ethyl contains EPA rather than an EPA/DHA combination.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Icosapent ethyl is a standardized prescription EPA product used to lower triglycerides; current guideline guidance distinguishes prescription omega-3 medications from variable-content nonprescription fish-oil supplements.
candidate.source_document_title: Icosapent Ethyl Capsules Prescribing Information; 2026 ACC/AHA Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
